facts.statement: Mengciusornis was a basal ornithuromorph dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Mengciusornis is an extinct genus of basal ornithuromorph dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Mengciusornis have been discovered in the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: remains of which have been found in the Jiufotang Formation.

facts.statement: Mengciusornis belongs to the family Schizoouridae, a group that also includes the closely related genus Schizooura.
facts.quote: Together with the closely related Schizooura it makes up the family Schizoouridae.

facts.statement: The genus Mengciusornis is represented by a single well-preserved skeleton specimen, IVPP V26275, which includes feather remains.
facts.quote: Mengciusornis is known from a single specimen, IVPP V26275, a well-preserved skeleton with remains of feathers.

facts.statement: Unlike its toothless relative Schizooura, Mengciusornis had large, curved teeth on its upper jaw.
facts.quote: Unlike its sister genus Schizooura, which was toothless, Mengciusornis possessed large, curved teeth on its premaxillae, similar to those of the distantly related Longipteryx.

facts.statement: The name Mengciusornis honors the Chinese philosopher Mencius, and its species name means "toothed" in Latin.
facts.quote: The generic name honours the Chinese philosopher Mencius, while the specific epithet is Latin for "toothed".

facts.statement: Mengciusornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
